models_evaluated: 33 models across four families (specialized neural models and frontier LLMs; individual names not given in text)

links.outcome: Whether aggregate external validation conceals subgroup performance disparities in CGM glucose forecasting
links.effect: Aggregate OOD metrics appeared stable (~1.0) while subgroup ratios ranged 0.8 to 1.4; T1D showed 6 mg/dL higher error than T2D (p<0.001), across all 33 models.
links.quote: Aggregate out-of-distribution metrics appear stable (approximately 1.0), yet subgroup-level ratios range from 0.8 to 1.4, with T1D patients showing 6 mg/dL higher prediction error than T2D (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Whether population-level validation reveals subgroup performance gaps versus subgroup-disaggregated analysis
links.effect: Population-level external validation concealed subgroup disparities (ratios 0.8 to 1.4; T1D vs T2D gap of 6 mg/dL, p<0.001) persisting across all 33 models.
links.quote: These findings establish that population-level validation alone is insufficient for equity assessment of digital health AI, motivating subgroup-disaggregated reporting as a default standard.

unlisted_practices: Personalized input-length configurations by demographic subgroup for CGM forecasting models

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating 33 models for glucose forecasting across demographic strata, directly demonstrating that subgroup-level validation uncovers hidden disparities masked by aggregate population-level validation.
